correctness.rationale: Smoothness iff a²≠4; degree-seven separable hyperelliptic polynomial yields genus three. The exact Hasse--Witt matrix over characteristic 13 is diag(B,A,B), B=2a²+6 and A=a⁶+4a⁴−a²−6, verified both by hand coefficient extraction and the standalone SymPy verifier. A=0 comprises six distinct quadratic-degree geometric parameters; B=0 comprises ±6; A and B are coprime and avoid the discriminant. Because the semilinear matrix is diagonal, its stable rank gives the claimed geometric p-ranks and its rank gives the a-numbers. Elliptic quotient maps and norm correspondence give a degree-nine isogeny with E0×E1², which supplies all Newton slopes. The prior primes 5,7,11 are handled by exact elliptic Hasse coefficients. No finite census stands in for the universal claims.

originality.rationale: Compared the mathematical statement with the full relevant Section 6 of Fuertes--Streit 2006, Section 3.1 of Gutierrez--Sevilla--Shaska 2012, the Achter--Pries hyperelliptic p-rank introduction, and accessible published-finding corpus and archived mathematical claims. The classical family, elliptic quotient geometry, and superspecial parameter zeros are old. Their mathematical implications do not include the complete characteristic-13 rank-one/rank-two Newton and a-number classification or the first-appearance assertion. Remaining priority risk is specifically unindexed elliptic/Cartier parameter tables and differently normalized historical results.

value.rationale: A sharp first-occurrence phenomenon in a classical one-dimensional genus-three dihedral family: the rank-one Newton stratum is empty at the smaller tame odd primes but consists of exactly two rational marked parameters in characteristic 13. The full rank-one/rank-two/ordinary boundary, all Newton polygons and exact degree-one/degree-two field counts are classified, and the exceptional magnitude is independently singled out in the historical complex uniformization. This is a natural arithmetic structural boundary rather than an unmotivated isolated invariant; the result deliberately does not claim a new global theorem.
